classification.difficultyReason: Rearrange and plot two inequalities, solve their boundary equations simultaneously and identify the common half-plane region, including cases where its bounding line changes across the intersection.

content.prompt: Sketch both inequalities on the same set of axes, shade the region of intersection and find the point of intersection of the two lines.

answer.short:
$y\ge2-\frac{x}{2}$ and $y<4-x$. Intersection: $(4,0)$.
The shaded area is the required region.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x+2y&\ge4\\y&\ge2-\frac{x}{2}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}2x+2y&<8\\y&<4-x\end{align*}$$
Draw the solid boundary through $(0,2)$ and $(4,0)$, and the dotted boundary through $(0,4)$ and $(4,0)$. Shade above the solid line and below the dotted line. The common region lies to the left of the intersection $(4,0)$. The intersection itself is excluded by the strict inequality.
The shaded area is the required region.

spec.description: Schematic axes without regular ticks or grid; solid and dotted boundaries and their common required region. Viewport is an authored plotting window.

answer.short:
$y\le3-\frac{3x}{4}$ and $y>3-3x$. Intersection: $(0,3)$.
The shaded area is the required region.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}3x+4y&\le12\\y&\le3-\frac{3x}{4}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}3x+y&>3\\y&>3-3x\end{align*}$$
Draw the solid boundary through $(0,3)$ and $(4,0)$, and the dotted boundary through $(0,3)$ and $(1,0)$. Shade below the solid line and above the dotted line. The common region lies to the right of $(0,3)$. The intersection is excluded by the strict inequality.
The shaded area is the required region.

spec.description: Solid shallow and dotted steep descending boundaries; common required region to their right. No regular ticks or grid; authored schematic viewport.

answer.short:
$y<\frac{2x}{3}-2$ and $y<x-2$. Shade below both dotted lines. Intersection: $(0,-2)$.
The shaded area is the required region.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2x-3y&>6\\-3y&>6-2x\\y&<\frac{2x}{3}-2\end{align*}$$
The inequality reverses when dividing by $-3$. Draw dotted boundaries through $(0,-2)$ and $(3,0)$, and through $(0,-2)$ and $(2,0)$. Shade below both lines. They intersect at $(0,-2)$, which is excluded from the required region.
The shaded area is the required region.

spec.description: Two dotted ascending boundaries and shading below both; no regular ticks or grid. Authored schematic viewport.

answer.short:
$y\ge\frac{3x}{5}-3$ and $y>3x-3$. Shade above both lines. Intersection: $(0,-3)$.
The shaded area is the required region.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}3x-5y&\le15\\-5y&\le15-3x\\y&\ge\frac{3x}{5}-3\end{align*}$$
The inequality reverses when dividing by $-5$.
$$\begin{align*}y-3x&>-3\\y&>3x-3\end{align*}$$
Draw the solid boundary through $(0,-3)$ and $(5,0)$, and the dotted boundary through $(0,-3)$ and $(1,0)$. Shade above both lines. They intersect at $(0,-3)$, which is excluded by the strict inequality.
The shaded area is the required region.

answer.short:
$y\ge-x+4$ and $y\ge2-\frac{2x}{3}$. Shade above both solid lines. Intersection: $(6,-2)$.
The shaded area is the required region.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2x+3y&\ge6\\y&\ge2-\frac{2x}{3}\end{align*}$$
Draw solid boundaries through $(0,4)$ and $(4,0)$, and through $(0,2)$ and $(3,0)$. Shade above both lines. Their intersection is $(6,-2)$ and is included in the required region.
The shaded area is the required region.

answer.short:
$y\le\frac{x}{2}+\frac{5}{2}$ and $y<10-x$. Shade below both lines. Intersection: $(5,5)$.
The shaded area is the required region.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2y-x&\le5\\y&\le\frac{x}{2}+\frac{5}{2}\end{align*}$$
Draw the solid boundary through $(-5,0)$ and $(0,2.5)$, and the dotted boundary through $(0,10)$ and $(10,0)$. Shade below both lines. They intersect at $(5,5)$, which is excluded by the strict inequality.
The shaded area is the required region.
